topics.title: 1.1 The impact of new and emerging technologies

outcomes.text: Weigh the effects of new technology on industry: unemployment, workforce skills, population movement and science parks.
Compare ways of starting a business: private ownership, crowd funding, government start-up funding, not-for-profits.
Explain how new technology affects transport costs, pollution, use of natural resources and waste.
Describe environmental effects of technology: pollution, waste disposal, materials separation, global transport and packaging.
Explain how new technology affects workers, consumers, children, disabled people, wages, skills and apprenticeships.
Describe cultural effects of technology, such as population movement in the EU and clustering within ethnic minorities.
Describe societal changes from technology: working hours, Internet of Things, remote working and video meetings.
Compare production approaches: standardised parts, just-in-time, lean manufacturing, batch, continuous, one-off and mass production.

topics.title: 1.2 Critical evaluation of new and emerging technologies

outcomes.text: Evaluate new technologies using budget, timescale, target user, materials and manufacturing ability to inform design decisions.
Use critical evaluation, including present and future scenarios such as disasters, medicine, travel, warming and communication, to guide design.
Judge new technologies ethically: where and by whom made, who benefits, and fair trade.
Judge new technologies environmentally: materials, carbon footprint, energy in making and transport, and life cycle analysis.
Describe how energy is generated and stored from fossil fuels, biofuels, tidal, wind, solar and hydroelectric sources.
Describe how systems are powered by batteries, solar cells, mains electricity and wind power.
Choose an energy source using portability, environmental impact, power output, connections and cost.

topics.title: 1.4 Modern and smart materials, composites and technical textiles

outcomes.text: Describe shape-memory alloys, nanomaterials, reactive glass, piezoelectric materials, temperature-responsive polymers and conductive inks and their uses.
Describe composites such as concrete, plywood, carbon and glass fibre, reinforced polymers and robotic materials.
Describe technical textiles: agro, construction, geo, domestic, environmentally friendly, protective and sports textiles.
Identify linear, reciprocating, rotary and oscillating movement.
Classify levers as class 1, 2 or 3 and calculate mechanical advantage, velocity ratio, load, effort and efficiency.
Describe bell crank and reverse motion linkages.
Describe pear-shaped, eccentric and drop (snail) cams.
Describe roller, knife and flat followers.
Describe V-belt pulleys and calculate velocity ratio and input and output speeds.
Describe how cranks and sliders work.
Describe simple and compound gear trains, idler and bevel gears, rack and pinion, and calculate RPM.
Explain the role of sensors, including light-dependent resistors and thermistors.
Explain the role of switches, transistors and resistors as control components.
Explain the role of outputs such as buzzers and LEDs.
Use flowcharts to plan how a programmed product behaves.
Switch outputs on and off in response to inputs and decisions.
Process and respond to analogue inputs.
Use simple routines with delays, loops and counts to control outputs.
Describe ferrous metals: mild steel, stainless steel and cast iron.
Describe non-ferrous metals: aluminium, copper and brass.
Explain metal properties: ductility, malleability and hardness.
Describe copier, cartridge and tracing papers.
Describe folding boxboard, corrugated board and solid white board.
Explain paper properties: flexibility, printability and biodegradability.
Describe thermoforming polymers: acrylic, HIPS and biodegradable Biopol.
Describe thermosetting polymers: polyester resin and urea formaldehyde.
Explain polymer properties: heat and electrical insulation and toughness.
Describe natural fibres such as wool and cotton.
Describe synthetic fibres such as polyester and acrylic.
Describe woven fabrics: plain calico and twill denim.
Describe non-woven fabrics: felted wool and bonded fibre webs.
Describe weft-knitted and warp-knitted fabrics.
Explain textile properties: elasticity, resilience and durability.
Describe hardwoods: oak, mahogany, beech and balsa.
Describe softwoods: pine and cedar.
Describe manufactured timbers: plywood and MDF.
Explain timber properties: hardness, toughness and durability.
Choose and justify materials, components and processes using their properties, advantages and disadvantages.
Respect the differing needs and values of social, ethnic and economic groups when finding design opportunities.
Explain environmental, social and economic issues in making products: fair trade, carbon offsetting, disassembly and disposal.
Describe the main factors of green design.
Describe the main factors of recycling and reusing materials or products.
Explain how human capability constrains design.
Explain how the cost of materials constrains design.
Explain how manufacturing capability constrains design.
Use life cycle analysis to judge environmental impact.
Analyse a product by form, function, user needs, performance, materials, production scale, sustainability, aesthetics, marketability and innovation.
Study the work of chosen past and present designers and companies.
Use design strategies such as collaboration, user-centred design and systems thinking to generate ideas and avoid fixation.
Present design ideas with sketches, annotation, models, photography, projections, drawings, schematics and CAD.
Record and justify design ideas clearly in writing.
Apply knowledge of metals, components and processes when designing or modifying a product.

topics.title: 2.2 Sources, properties and footprint of metals

outcomes.text: Describe high carbon steel and tungsten steel alongside mild and stainless steel and cast iron.
Describe tin, 7000 series aluminium and titanium alongside aluminium, copper and brass.
Say where iron ore, steel, bauxite, copper and tin are sourced around the world.
Compare conductivity, magnetism and density of metals.
Compare working properties of metals: durability, toughness, elasticity, tensile and compressive strength.
Explain the social footprint of metals: trends, effects on communities and wildlife, recycling.
Explain the ecological footprint of metals: extraction, erosion, processing, transport, waste, pollution.
Explain how form, colour and texture influence metal choice.
Explain environmental factors in metal choice, including steel energy use and corrosion.
Explain how stock and specialist material availability and market price affect metal choice.
Explain how quality, processing, metal exchange price and recycling cost affect metal cost.
Explain how social groups, fashion and popularity affect metal choice.
Explain cultural and ethical factors: offence, target market, consumerism, mass production and obsolescence.
Describe compression, tension, shear, electrical and magnetic forces and stresses on metals.
Describe hardening, tempering, carbon content, work hardening and I, U, T and C beams.
Describe metal stock forms: bar, sheet, plate, tube, castings, extrusions, wire and powder metallurgy.
Use gauge, cross-sectional area, diameter and tube wall thickness to work out quantities.
Compare forging, casting, powder metallurgy, stamping, welding, extrusion and hardening.
Match one-off, batch, mass and continuous production to metal products.
Use marking out, jigs, fixtures, templates, patterns, moulds, CAM, quality control, tolerance and efficient cutting for quantity production.
Choose hand tools, machinery and digital design and manufacture for metal.
Describe shaping metal by filing, cutting, drilling, turning, milling, bending, grinding, casting and reforming.
Describe joining metal by welding, brazing, soldering, stamping, punching, riveting and sheet metalwork.
Describe assembling metal with threads, nuts and bolts, machine screws and adhesives.
Compare metal finishes: paint, dip coating, electroplating, anodising, galvanising, powder coating, lacquer and polishing.
Apply knowledge of papers, boards, components and processes when designing or modifying a product.

topics.title: 3.2 Sources, properties and footprint of papers and boards

outcomes.text: Describe bond paper and heat transfer printing paper.
Describe foil-lined board.
Describe packaging laminates such as Tetra Pak: paperboard, polyethylene and foil.
Say where pulp, paper, cardboard and rice paper come from.
Compare density, transparency and texture of papers and boards.
Compare working properties: weight, surface finish, printability and absorbency.
Explain the social footprint: trends, logging effects, ethical disposal, reduced packaging and brand identity.
Explain the ecological footprint: harvesting, erosion, processing, transport, waste and pollution.

subtopics.title: Factors in choosing paper and board

outcomes.text: Explain how form, colour, texture and surface graphics influence choice.
Explain environmental factors: sustainability, pollution and genetic engineering.
Explain how stock and specialist material availability affects choice.
Explain cost factors: quality, decoration, processing, commodity price and recycling cost.
Explain how social groups, fashion and popularity affect choice.
Explain cultural and ethical factors including colour and language, consumerism and obsolescence.

topics.title: 3.4 Forces and stresses on papers and boards

outcomes.text: Describe bending, torsion, shear and compression on papers and boards.
Describe laminating, encapsulation, corrugation, layers and ribs, sandwich construction and packaging laminates.

topics.title: 3.5 Paper and board stock forms and sizes

outcomes.text: Describe paper and board stock forms: weights, bond and laminates.
Use A, B, foolscap, letter and envelope sizes, area and diameter to work out quantities.
Compare printing, cutting, intermediate, frame and test modelling.
Match one-off, batch, mass and continuous production to paper products.
Use marking out, folding jigs, fixtures, templates, patterns, stencils, photocopying, CAM, quality control, tolerance and efficient cutting.
Choose hand tools, machinery and digital design and manufacture for paper and board.
Describe shaping by cutting, folding, notching, modelling and manipulation.
Describe strengthening, adding windows and inserts, lamination, pins, stapling, taping, paper engineering, adhesives, lettering, binding and marking-out tools.
Compare varnishing, hot foil blocking, edge staining, embossing, UV varnish and laminates and films.
Apply knowledge of polymers, components and processes when designing or modifying a product.

topics.title: 4.2 Sources, properties and footprint of polymers

outcomes.text: Describe polystyrene, Styrofoam, PVC, ABS, PET, polyurethane and fluoroelastomer.
Describe polyester resin used with glass and carbon fibre, and urea formaldehyde.
Say where crude oil for polymers is sourced.
Compare density and durability of polymers.
Compare working properties: heat and electrical insulation, toughness, plasticity, hardness, tensile and compressive strength.
Explain the social footprint: trends, environmental and wildlife impact, recycling difficulty.
Explain the ecological footprint: oil extraction, wildlife loss, processing, transport, waste and pollution.
Explain how form, colour and texture influence polymer choice.
Explain environmental factors: sustainability, pollution and Biopol.
Explain how stock, specialist supply and global oil supply affect choice.
Explain cost factors: quality, processing, fire proofing, additives and world oil price.
Explain how social groups, fashion and popularity affect choice.
Explain cultural and ethical factors including colour and language, consumerism and obsolescence.
Describe compression, tension, shear and flexibility in polymers.
Describe frame structures, triangulation, suitable construction processes and additives.
Describe polymer stock forms: bar, sheet, tube, mouldings, resin, granules and film.
Use thickness, cross-sectional area, sheet size and diameter to work out quantities.
Compare blow moulding, press moulding, extrusion, injection moulding, polymer welding and line bending.
Match one-off, batch, mass and continuous production to polymer products.
Use marking out, jigs, templates, patterns, moulds, CAM, quality control, tolerance and efficient cutting.
Choose hand tools, machinery and digital design and manufacture for polymers.
Describe laser cutting, cutting, filing, bending, abrading, vacuum forming and reforming.
Describe tapping, fastening and adhesives such as epoxy resin and solvent cements, plus wastage and addition.
Compare polishing, textured moulds, laser engraving, vinyl stickers and GRP pigments.
Apply knowledge of materials, components and processes when designing or modifying a system.

topics.title: 5.2 Sources, properties and footprint of components

outcomes.text: Describe moisture and piezoelectric sensors alongside LDRs and thermistors.
Describe switches (PTM, micro, reed), variable resistors, bipolar transistors, microprocessors, PICs and relays.
Describe loudspeakers and motors as outputs alongside buzzers and LEDs.
Say where polymers, silicon, gold, copper, lithium, aluminium, rare earths and nickel come from.
Read resistor colour codes, tolerances and ratings, and choose materials for cases.
Compare conductors and insulators and the properties of polymers used for cases.
Explain social footprint: scarce or hazardous elements and effects of communications devices and social media.
Explain ecological footprint: extraction, obsolescence, use and toxic disposal.
Explain how form, colour and texture influence enclosure choice.
Explain the RoHS and WEEE directives for selection and disposal.
Explain how stock, specialist supply and scarce elements affect choice.
Explain how component tolerances and manufacturing processes affect cost.
Explain how social groups, fashion and popularity affect choice.
Explain cultural and ethical factors including colour and language, consumerism and obsolescence.
Describe tension, compression, torsion and shear on objects.
Describe composites and ribbing to strengthen case structures.
Describe E12 resistors, tolerances and values, surface-mount and through-hole components.
Use amp, ohm and volt, Ohm's law, series and parallel resistor formulas, area and diameter.
Describe photo etching, and PCB drilling and soldering.
Match breadboard prototyping, batch, mass and continuous production to systems.
Use pick and place, SMT, quality control, marking out, templates, patterns, sub-assembly, tolerance and efficient cutting.
Choose hand tools, machinery and digital design and manufacture for systems.
Describe vacuum forming, CNC laser cutting, 3D printing and drilling.
Describe through-hole and surface-mount PCB mounting and cable management with looms, sleeving and ties.
Describe metal plating, insulating coatings, resistor colour bands and case finishes such as anodising, painting and screen printing.
Apply knowledge of textiles, components and processes when designing or modifying a product.

outcomes.text: Describe silk and linen alongside wool and cotton.
Describe regenerated cellulosic fibres, polyamide, elastane and nylon alongside polyester and acrylic.
Describe satin jacquard and pile velvet fabrics alongside plain and twill weaves.
Describe non-woven felted and bonded fabrics.
Describe weft-knitted and warp-knitted fabrics.

Describe textile stock forms: rolls, blocks, denier, single and double weights, laminates.

Compare shears, stamping, laser cutting, heated cutters and extrusion.
Match one-off, batch, mass and continuous production to textile products.

outcomes.text: Describe jelutong, birch and ash hardwoods.
Describe larch softwood.
Describe chipboard alongside plywood and MDF.
Say where Alpine, European and Amazonian timbers come from.
Compare timber knots, colour, grain and density.

Explain how stock and specialist supply, hurricanes, storms and disease affect availability.

Describe timber stock forms: regular sections, mouldings, dowels and sheets.
